Bulgarian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [sam]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -am

Etymology 1

[edit]
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *sem-
Proto-Indo-European *somHós
Proto-Slavic *samъ
Bulgarian сам

    Inherited from Proto-Slavic *samъ.

    Adjective

    [edit]

    сам • (sam) (adverb са́мо)

    1. alone, by oneself
    2. the very ..., the ... himself/herself/itself
      на сами́я край
      na samíja kraj
      at the very end
      сама́та жена́ дойде́
      samáta žená dojdé
      the woman herself came

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

    Inherited from Old Church Slavonic сѣмъ (sěmŭ), an oblique case form of сѣмо (sěmo, “here, hither”), from Proto-Slavic *sěmo. The unexpected vowel in modern Bulgarian is likely by analogy with там (tam, “there”) and its derived terms.

    Adverb

    [edit]

    сам • (sam) (not comparable) (archaic or dialectal)

    1. with beckoning verbs in the imperative: here, in this place
      Ела́ сам! ― Elá sam! ― Come here!
    Derived terms
    [edit]
    • наса́м (nasám)
    • отса́м (otsám)

    Pannonian Rusyn

    [edit]

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): [ˈsam]
    • Rhymes: -am
    • Hyphenation: сам

    Etymology 1

    [edit]

    Inherited from Old Slovak sám, from Proto-Slavic *samъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *sāmas, from Proto-Indo-European *somHós.

    Pronoun

    [edit]

    сам (sam)

    1. self, oneself
      сaм нє знам цо ми було ― sam nje znam co mi bulo ― I myself don't know what happened to me

    Adjective

    [edit]

    сам (sam) (not comparable, abstract noun самота)

    1. alone, solitary, lonely, secluded, on one's lonesome (by oneself without company)
      Synonym: осамени (osameni)
      нашол сом го самого дома ― našol som ho samoho doma ― I found him alone at home
    2. alone, singlehanded (by oneself without help)
      Synonym: поєдинєчни (pojedinječni)
      мушиш сам себе помогнуц ― mušiš sam sebe pomohnuc ― you alone must help yourself
    Declension
    [edit]

    dative самому (samomu) самей (samej) самому (samomu) самим (samim)
    accusative personal/animal inanimate саму (samu) само / саме (samo / same) самих (samix) сами (sami)

    vocative сам (sam) сама (sama) само / саме (samo / same) сами (sami)

    Adverb

    [edit]

    сам (sam)

    1. alone (by oneself without company)
    2. alone, singlehandedly (by oneself without help)
      Synonyms: без помоци (bez pomoci), поєдинєчно (pojedinječno)

    Noun

    [edit]

    сам (sam) m pers (feminine equivalent сама)

    1. (nominalized) bachelor, single man (man who is not married, who lives alone)
      Synonym: самец (samec)

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

    Inherited from Old Slovak samý.

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • сами (sami) — in the nominative singular

    Adjective

    [edit]

    сам (sam) (not comparable)

    1. denotes spatial or temporal proximity; the very, right, oneself
      по саме шерцо ― po same šerco ― to the very heart
      вишли на сам верх гори ― višli na sam verx hori ― they went to the very top of the mountain
      биваю при самим беґелю ― bivaju pri samim begelju ― they live right next to the canal
      то було на сам Крачун ― to bulo na sam Kračun ― that was on Christmas day itself
    2. emphasizes the utmost measure of a trait
      кукурица сами цирок и сама тараска ― kukurica sami cirok i sama taraska ― corn is God's own sorghum and millet

    Russian

    [edit]

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • самъ (sam) — pre-1918 spelling

    Etymology

    [edit]

      Inherited from Old East Slavic самъ (samŭ), from Proto-Slavic *samъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *sāmas, from Proto-Indo-European *somHós.

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): [sam]
      • Audio:(file)

      Pronoun

      [edit]

      сам • (sam) m (neuter само́, feminine сама́, plural са́ми)

      1. (definitive pronoun, emphatic) self, -self
        Я сам э́то ви́дел.
        Ja sam éto vídel.
        I saw it myself.
        Само́ госуда́рство так реши́ло.
        Samó gosudárstvo tak rešílo.
        The State itself has so decided.
      2. (regional, Ukraine, numeral, emphatic) alone
        Я сам гуляю.
        Ja sam guljaju.
        I am strolling alone.

      Declension

      [edit]
      Declension of сам
      masculine neuter feminine plural
      nominative сам
      sam       		само́

      Serbo-Croatian

      [edit]

      Etymology 1

      [edit]

      Inherited from Proto-Slavic *samъ.

      Adjective

      [edit]

      са̑м (Latin spelling sȃm, definite са̑мӣ)

      1. alone, sole
      2. the very
      3. unaided, single-handed
      4. absolute, mere, unmixed
      5. solitary, secluded

      Etymology 2

      [edit]

      Inherited from Proto-Slavic *(j)esmь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *esmi, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁es-.

      Verb

      [edit]

      са̏м (Latin spelling sȁm)

      1. first-person singular present enclitic of би̏ти
        Ту сам. ― I'm here.

      Southern Yukaghir

      [edit]

      Alternative forms

      [edit]
      • саам (sām)

      Etymology

      [edit]

      Borrowed from Russian сам (sam).

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): [ˈsam]
      • Rhymes: -am
      • Hyphenation: сам

      Pronoun

      [edit]

      сам (sam)

      1. self, -self
        • 2007, M. I. Turpanova, Раньше, когда мы были маленькие [Before, when we were little]:
          Титтэ сам иҥдьэҥитэй, - мони.
          Titte sam iŋdʹeŋitej, - moni.
          They will sew it themselves, - he said.

      References

      [edit]
      • Elena Maslova (2003), A Grammar of Kolyma Yukaghir, Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter, →ISBN, page 26
